title: Nectarous Japanese Apricots Soup
description: A resinous, springy soup that balances sweet dried apricots with the subtle smokiness of binchotan charcoal, perfect for a Kanto-style vegan lunch.
instructions: Rinse the soaked dried apricots and reserve the soaking liquid.
Combine the apricots, soaking liquid, water, and kombu in a pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Let the broth simmer for 20 minutes, skimming off any foam that rises to the surface.
Remove the kombu and add the lightly toasted binchotan charcoal, allowing it to infuse for 3 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce, mirin, and sesame oil, then simmer the mixture for an additional 5 minutes.
Blend the soup until smooth, then strain it through a fine sieve to remove any solids.
Return the strained soup to the pot and heat it to just below boiling to preserve the delicate flavors.
Taste the soup and adjust the seasoning with more soy sauce if necessary.
Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with sliced scallions.
Serve the soup hot, enjoying the sweet apricot aroma mingled with the subtle smokiness.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
